q: A mercy order is passed in favour of a donor of the ruling party on materials shown to be irrelevant. Which statement is correct?
options: The order may be set aside, clemency being reviewable on limited grounds
The order stands, clemency being an act of grace beyond judicial scrutiny
The order stands unless the convict concerned was sentenced to death
The order may be set aside only by the successor in that office
expl: Mala fides, irrelevant considerations and non-application of mind are all reviewable grounds.
why: The leading authority on this point arose in Andhra Pradesh, which makes it doubly relevant for a State paper.
trapnote: Clemency is wide but not lawless. The reviewable grounds are limited but real.

q: Consider: 1-A Governor may pardon an offence against a law relating to a State subject. 2-A Governor may pardon a sentence passed by a court martial. 3-A Governor may commute a death sentence. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Court martial sentences lie outside a Governor's power; commutation of a death sentence does not.
why: The three statements separate subject-matter, type of court and type of relief, which are three different axes.
trapnote: Three axes: which law, which court, which relief. A Governor fails on the court martial axis.

q: An ordinance is allowed to lapse and an identical ordinance is issued the next day, repeatedly, over several years. Which statement is correct?
options: The practice is permissible where the legislature has not had time to consider the matter
The practice is permissible provided each ordinance is separately notified
The practice is a fraud on the Constitution and the ordinances are liable to be struck down
The practice is impermissible only where the subject matter is a State subject
expl: Systematic re-promulgation without legislative consideration subverts the legislative process.
why: The second option states the narrow exception that was contemplated and presents it as the general rule.
trapnote: A narrow exception presented as a general rule is the standard way this case is misstated.

q: A Concurrent-list State Bill repugnant to an earlier Union law is reserved and receives Presidential assent. Effect on repugnancy?
options: Assent cures repugnancy and the State law prevails in that State
Reservation itself kills the Bill
Governor must have assented instead
State can override without assent
expl: Presidential assent after reservation cures repugnancy for that State.
why: Reservation exists precisely for repugnancy and constitutional doubt. Assent, not reservation alone, resolves it.
trapnote: Reservation is the route; assent is the cure.

q: A Council of Ministers in a State with an Assembly of sixty members is proposed to consist of eleven ministers. Which statement is correct?
options: Impermissible, the Council must consist of at least twelve ministers in every State
Permissible, the floor of twelve applying only where fifteen per cent would be lower
Permissible, fifteen per cent of sixty being nine and the proposal exceeding it
Impermissible, fifteen per cent of sixty being nine and the proposal exceeding it
expl: The State floor is twelve, so a Council of eleven falls below the prescribed minimum.
why: Two options compute the percentage correctly and then ignore the floor, which is the trap in this item.
trapnote: The percentage is a ceiling and the floor of twelve is a separate minimum for States.

q: Consider: 1-The President is part of Parliament. 2-A Governor is part of the State legislature. 3-The Vice-President is part of Parliament. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The President and a Governor are constituents of their legislatures; the Vice-President is not.
why: The Vice-President presides over a House without being a constituent element of Parliament.
trapnote: Presiding over a House is not the same as being a constituent part of the legislature.

q: A Governor reserves a Bill that would derogate from the powers of the High Court. Which statement is correct?
options: Reservation is available but never obligatory in any category of Bill
Reservation is obligatory only where the Bill is a Money Bill
Reservation is obligatory in such a case, not merely available
Reservation is obligatory only where the President has so instructed
expl: Where a Bill would derogate from the powers of the High Court, reservation is compulsory.
why: Most summaries present reservation as purely discretionary, which is why the obligatory category is tested.
trapnote: Reservation is usually discretionary but compulsory in one specified category.

q: Consider the power to grant a pardon: 1-It may be exercised before conviction. 2-It may be exercised after conviction. 3-It extinguishes both the conviction and the sentence. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: It operates after conviction and, being a pardon, removes conviction and sentence alike.
why: Pardon is distinguished from commutation, remission, respite and reprieve by the fact that it wipes the conviction.
trapnote: Pardon removes the conviction itself. The other four forms of clemency affect only the sentence.

q: A State legislature is not in session and the Governor promulgates an ordinance which is never laid before the House. Which statement is correct?
options: The failure to lay it is itself an abuse of the ordinance-making power
The failure to lay it is a procedural irregularity of no legal consequence
The ordinance continues in force until expressly repealed by the House
The failure to lay it is excused where the House sits for fewer than six weeks
expl: Laying the ordinance before the House is a mandatory constitutional obligation.
why: The fourth option invents an exception based on the length of the session, which sounds administratively plausible.
trapnote: Laying is mandatory. The six-week period governs expiry, not the duty to lay.

q: A President returns a Bill; the Houses re-pass it; a Governor reserves a different Bill; the President returns it and the State House re-passes it. Which statement is correct?
options: The President must assent to both Bills once they are re-passed
The President need not assent to either Bill after re-passage
The President must assent to the second; he need not assent to the first
The President must assent to the first; he need not assent to the second
expl: Re-passage compels assent at the Union level but not on a Bill reserved by a Governor.
why: The asymmetry between the two routes is the entire point, and three options deny it in different ways.
trapnote: Two routes, two different consequences of re-passage. The asymmetry is deliberate.
